sources_append: Angsinco-Jimenez et al., 2003; Fortes, 2013; Sanchez-Delute et al., 2025, as cited in docs/11-species.md.
transcript:
This is spoon seagrass, Halophila ovalis. A display, not a scan of a meadow in Mati.

The leaves arise in pairs. Each leaf is an oval, larger than the small spoon seagrass beside it. There are no hairs on the surface.

Count across the leaf. There are eight or more cross veins. Halophila minor has fewer than eight. That is the difference to remember.

It is a common early coloniser, so a new patch can appear on open ground. After that, the buried stem spreads the patch. Roots grow down at the nodes. It can also flower and set seed.
